chunks: And Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a slave who was jointly owned by two men. One of them freed his half while the slave was still a child, and the other retained ownership of his half. He said: "He shall be valued at the worth of the day the first [owner] freed [his share], and the freed slave is ordered to work to pay off the half that was not freed until he fulfills it."
ai.seo_question: How is the value of a partially freed slave calculated when ownership was split?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial liability in partial manumission, establishing that the redemption price is fixed at the slave's value at the moment of the first emancipation, preventing inflation of the debt due to the owner's delay. It underscores the practical mechanism of 'kittabah' (contract of manumission) where the slave works off the remaining half, reflecting the Shia emphasis on facilitating freedom through equitable legal structures.
